_meta.credit: Spelling patterns follow the national curriculum in England, English Appendix 1 (DfE, 2013). Contains public sector information licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0. The wording and example words are Waystead's own.
_meta.note: Each word must match its pattern's `re` and be on our lists: tests/grownups.test.js checks.

patterns.title: Doubling before an ending
patterns.rule: When the last part of a longer word is stressed, its last letter doubles before -ing, -ed or -er.

patterns.title: No doubling before an ending
patterns.rule: When the last part is not stressed, the last letter stays single.

patterns.title: y that sounds like short i
patterns.rule: In some words the short i sound is spelled y.

patterns.title: ou that sounds like u
patterns.rule: In some words the u sound in cup is spelled ou.

patterns.title: Prefixes dis- and mis-
patterns.rule: dis- and mis- change a word to mean the opposite, or done wrongly.

patterns.title: Prefixes in-, il-, im- and ir-
patterns.rule: All mean not. Before l it's il-, before m or p it's im-, before r it's ir-.

patterns.title: Prefixes re- and sub-
patterns.rule: re- means again or back; sub- means under.

patterns.title: Prefixes inter-, super-, anti- and auto-
patterns.rule: inter- means between, super- above, anti- against and auto- self.

patterns.title: Ending -ation
patterns.rule: -ation turns a verb into a noun.

patterns.title: Ending -ly
patterns.rule: -ly turns an adjective into an adverb. A word ending in y changes it to i first.

patterns.title: Endings -sure and -ture
patterns.rule: These endings sound like zher and cher.

patterns.title: Ending -ous
patterns.rule: -ous makes an adjective. Sometimes the word before it changes.

patterns.title: Endings -tion, -sion, -ssion and -cian
patterns.rule: These all sound like shun. The word it comes from gives a clue.

patterns.title: ch that sounds like k
patterns.rule: In words from Greek, ch often sounds like k.

patterns.title: ch that sounds like sh
patterns.rule: In words from French, ch can sound like sh.

patterns.title: Endings -que and -gue
patterns.rule: Words from French can end in -que (k) or -gue (g).

patterns.title: sc that sounds like s
patterns.rule: In some words from Latin, sc sounds like s.

patterns.title: ei, eigh and ey that sound like ay
patterns.rule: Three spellings of the same long a sound.

patterns.title: Endings -cious and -tious
patterns.rule: Both sound like shus. If the root word ends in ce it's usually -cious.

patterns.title: Endings -cial and -tial
patterns.rule: Both sound like shul. -cial often follows a vowel, -tial a consonant.

patterns.title: Endings -ant, -ance and -ancy
patterns.rule: Use the a forms when a related word has a clear a sound.

patterns.title: Endings -ent, -ence and -ency
patterns.rule: Use the e forms after a soft c or g, or when a related word has a clear e sound.

patterns.title: Endings -able and -ably
patterns.rule: Often added to a whole word. Keep the e after a soft c or g.

patterns.title: Endings -ible and -ibly
patterns.rule: Often added when the rest isn't a whole word.

patterns.title: Words ending in -fer
patterns.rule: The r doubles when the -fer part stays stressed.

patterns.title: ie, and ei after c
patterns.rule: i before e, except after c when the sound is ee.

patterns.title: ough
patterns.rule: One of the trickiest letter strings: it has many sounds.

patterns.title: Silent letters
patterns.rule: Letters you can't hear, but need to write.
